title: U.S. House · Idaho's 2nd District
area: Eastern Idaho, including Idaho Falls, Pocatello, Twin Falls, and Boise's eastern portion.

context.text: Incumbent Michael K. Simpson defeated Brian Keene and Perry Shumway in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 63.3% of the vote. Elinor Gilbreath defeated Julie Wiley (who unofficially withdrew) in the Democratic primary with 72.5% of the vote. Will Johanson advanced from the Libertarian primary; Idaho Law (Constitution Party) is listed as withdrawn or disqualified and does not appear in the general election.
The Cook Political Report rates this district R+13 by partisan voting index.

summary.text: Mike Simpson is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Idaho's 2nd District, serving since 1999 and now in his fourteenth term. Born in Burley and raised in Blackfoot, he worked as a dentist, served on the Blackfoot City Council and in the Idaho Legislature, and was Speaker of the Idaho House before his election to Congress. He chairs the House Appropriations subcommittee on Interior and Environment.

background.text: Born in Burley, Idaho, and raised in Blackfoot, where his father was a dentist.

Graduated from Blackfoot High School, Utah State University (1972) and the Washington University School of Dental Medicine in St. Louis (1977), according to Wikipedia; his official biography confirms the university and dental degrees.
Practiced dentistry in Blackfoot, joining his father and uncle at the Simpson Family Dental Practice.
Began his political career in 1980 when he was elected to the Blackfoot City Council.
Served in the Idaho Legislature from 1984 to 1998, including his last six years as Speaker of the Idaho House.
Elected to the U.S. House in 1998 and took office in January 1999; his official biography says he is serving his fourteenth term.

Sits on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Interior and Environment Subcommittee and is a member of the Energy and Water Development and Labor, Health and Human Services, Education subcommittees.
According to his official biography, he has been married to his wife Kathy for more than 50 years, and the couple has lived in Idaho their whole lives.

priorities.text: Says he continuously opposed proposals to grant amnesty to illegal aliens and has worked to increase funding to combat illegal immigration and expedite the construction of a border fence.

Says he is troubled by the growing federal debt and supports drastically reducing discretionary spending, reforming entitlement programs, and passing a balanced-budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
Says the country should pursue a comprehensive energy strategy that includes nuclear power, energy efficiency, and renewable energy alongside continued development of oil and natural gas.

positions.summary: Says he has supported legislation allowing law enforcement to keep weapons, narcotics, and smugglers out of the country and to expedite the removal of criminal aliens, and has worked to increase funding to combat illegal immigration.
positions.quote: I have supported legislation which allows law enforcement to do what is necessary to keep harmful weapons, narcotics, and smugglers out of our country and expedites the removal of criminal aliens.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025-2026 Congress, chairing the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee, and also sitting on the Labor-HHS-Education and Energy-Water Development subcommittees.
Chaired the Interior and Environment appropriations subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress and served as ranking member of the Energy and Water Development subcommittee in 2021-2022.

candidates.name: Elinor Gilbreath

summary.text: Elinor (Ellie) Gilbreath is the Democratic nominee for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. A Georgetown-trained attorney, she has worked as a mediator and coach and has lived in the Ketchum area for about 23 years. She has not held elected office and describes herself as a political centrist.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Los Angeles.
Earned a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center and is a trained attorney.
Has more than 20 years of experience in conflict resolution and mediation, according to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
Owns and operates a business and personal coaching business under her maiden name, Ellie Newman Coaching, according to the Idaho Mountain Express.
According to EastIdahoNews.com, her family moved to Idaho in 2003 with their 18-month-old daughter; she is a Ketchum resident of 23 years.
Has never held an elected position, according to the Idaho Mountain Express.

Entered the Democratic primary shortly before the filing deadline; fellow candidate Julie Wiley endorsed her and later suspended her campaign, and Gilbreath became the Democratic nominee. She describes herself as a "political centrist."

priorities.text: Says her priorities are restoring accountability and balance in government, protecting Idaho's public lands, water, and energy, and lowering the cost of living for Idaho families, including access to affordable healthcare.
Says she will focus on protecting fundamental freedoms and ensuring government works for everyone rather than special interests.
priorities.quote: From freedom of speech to the Second Amendment, I believe upholding the rule of law and that laws must be applied evenly and lawfully—without favoritism, political weaponization, or selective enforcement.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions in her survey (e.g. on public lands, healthcare costs) did not map cleanly to the guide's fixed issue list without inferring specifics, so no Position entries were added; priorities are recorded instead.

candidates.name: Will Johanson

summary.text: Will Johanson is the Libertarian Party nominee for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he grew up in California's Central Valley, served in the U.S. Navy as a nuclear operator, and now works as an engineer in Idaho's semiconductor industry. He advanced from the Libertarian primary on May 19, 2026.

background.text: According to his campaign website, was born and raised in California's Central Valley and says his interest in liberty began during Ron Paul's 2008 presidential campaign.
Enlisted in the U.S. Navy as a nuclear operator and served aboard the USS Georgia as an Engineering Laboratory Technician; he separated in 2020 as a Machinist's Mate (Nuclear) First Class (E-6).
Used the GI Bill to earn bachelor's and master's degrees in Materials Science & Engineering from Boise State University, according to his campaign website.
Works as an engineer in Idaho's semiconductor industry; his campaign is headquartered in Boise.

candidates.name: Emre Houser

summary.text: Emre Houser is an independent candidate for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he served more than 27 years in the Air Force and Idaho National Guard, including a deployment to Iraq, and has owned a small business in Idaho for more than 15 years. He says he was a registered Democrat until changing to unaffiliated in 2025.

background.text: According to his campaign website, joined the U.S. Air Force in 1995 and was stationed at Mountain Home Air Force Base after technical school in March 1996.
Deployed to Saudi Arabia and Bahrain on active duty, then joined the Idaho National Guard in Boise in 1999, with multiple deployments including Operation Iraqi Freedom in March 2003.
Describes more than 27 years of military service and more than 15 years as an Idaho small business owner, and says he has made Idaho his home for nearly 30 years.
Says he was a registered Democrat and was recruited to run as one, then changed his registration to Unaffiliated in 2025.

candidates.name: Tripp Hutchinson

summary.text: Tripp Hutchinson is an independent candidate for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District and a member of the Ketchum City Council, serving since 2024. According to his campaign website, he is Idaho born and raised. In 2026 he was sentenced on a misdemeanor petit theft charge; he is running on cost of living, rural land protection and term limits.

background.text: Describes himself as a born and raised Idaho local; his full name is Tripp Charles Hutchinson.
Has served on the Ketchum City Council since 2024 and said he does not plan to step down while campaigning.
Announced in early 2026 that he would run as an independent against incumbent Republican Mike Simpson, which required 500 signatures to qualify.

In March 2026 was sentenced in Fifth District Court on one count of misdemeanor petit theft after a plea agreement, over removing posters from a case at Friedman Memorial Airport; the judge imposed 12 months of probation and 40 hours of community service and withheld judgment until March 31, 2027. He described the act as "moral civil disobedience" and said he would accept the consequences.
According to his campaign website, his platform focuses on lowering the cost of living for working-class Idahoans, keeping Idaho rural, and opposing the consolidation of power.
